described_as.text: The party's 2025 manifesto is subtitled "Onze keuzes voor een fatsoenlijk land" ("Our choices for a decent country"). Its foreword says: "Wij kiezen voor een politiek die eerlijk is over wat moet en hoopvol over wat kan" ("We choose a politics that is honest about what must be done and hopeful about what is possible").

The reference site Parlement.com describes the CDA as a Christian-inspired party in the centre of the political spectrum, whose statement of principles approaches political questions in a Christian-democratic way and sees people as stewards of the created world.

The Documentation Centre for Dutch Political Parties (DNPP, University of Groningen) notes that the party was in government in 1977-1994, 2002-2012 and from 2017, and that its House seat total ranged from 54 in 1989 to 5 in 2023.

history.event: The Anti-Revolutionary Party (ARP), the Christian Historical Union (CHU) and the Catholic People's Party (KVP) formed a federation on 23 June 1973; in 1977 they contested a national election on one list for the first time, led by Dries van Agt, who became prime minister.
The CDA was founded on 11 October 1980 as the merger of ARP, CHU and KVP.
Under Ruud Lubbers the CDA was the largest party in the 1986 and 1989 elections, reaching 54 seats in 1989.

Lost 20 seats, at the time the largest loss in Dutch parliamentary history, and went into opposition; according to Parlement.com it was the first time since 1918 that no Christian party was in government.
Governed in four cabinets under Prime Minister Jan Peter Balkenende. In 2010 the party lost 20 seats and entered a minority cabinet with the VVD supported from outside by the PVV.
Won 19 seats under Sybrand van Haersma Buma and joined the Rutte III cabinet; in 2021, under Wopke Hoekstra, it won 15 seats and joined Rutte IV. MP Pieter Omtzigt left the party on 12 June 2021.

Henri Bontenbal became House group leader on 5 September 2023 and lead candidate; the party won 5 seats, its lowest result, losing many voters to BBB and NSC according to Parlement.com. It was in opposition from 2 July 2024.
Won 18 seats in the House election, 13 more than in 2023.

manifesto_2025.title: Bouwen op vertrouwen. Onze keuzes voor een fatsoenlijk land ("Building on trust. Our choices for a decent country") - Verkiezingsprogramma 2025

key_points.text: Build 100,000 homes a year, extend the principle of 'an extra street' to 'an extra neighbourhood' for villages and towns, and limit the possibilities to delay housing construction through legal procedures, including appeals to the Council of State.
Phase out the hypotheekrenteaftrek (mortgage interest tax relief) step by step while lowering income tax by the same amount, with the proceeds used one-for-one for lower income tax.

Introduce a levy on actual returns in box 3 (the tax on savings and investments) as soon as possible, so that tax is no longer charged on value 'locked up in bricks', with a temporary measure for small private landlords until then.

A new international asylum system in which applications are made outside Europe; rejected asylum seekers who do not cooperate with return commit a criminal offence. The party wants to implement the Spreidingswet (the law distributing asylum reception across municipalities) to end the use of expensive hotels for reception.

Statushouders (asylum seekers granted a residence permit) must complete civic integration or lose their status; labour migrants who stay longer follow a mandatory language course; asylum seekers with good prospects get access to the labour market after one month.

Reverse the planned reduction of the eigen risico (the compulsory health-insurance excess), which the manifesto says only makes premiums more expensive, while supporting a cap per treatment and attention to costs for the chronically ill. Simple care is to be organised regionally and complex care concentrated; a broad sugar tax is introduced.

Raise child benefit and the child budget and merge them into one scheme, introduce one more generous paid-leave scheme for both parents in a child's first year, make childcare almost free, and require an age check for social media.

Invest in defence as agreed at the NATO summit in The Hague, partly financed by a 'vrijheidsbijdrage' (freedom contribution) from citizens and businesses, and restore the obligation to report for military service (opkomstplicht).

Follow the European climate targets and adapt the Dutch Climate Act to them, scrap the national CO2 levy on industry, make binding agreements with the largest polluters, and choose a mix of renewable energy, nuclear energy, energy saving and CO2 storage, continuing the development of two new nuclear plants.
Work to meet the nitrogen targets while setting norms to be met in 2035 and before, and re-establish the nitrogen fund to give farmers prospects.
Confiscate criminal money and reinvest it in affected neighbourhoods, and end the regulated cannabis experiment, levying a cannabis tax while it runs.
A quota on motions in the House, a requirement that all political parties are internally democratic, and a Senate elected in two halves (38 and 37 members) every three years with a six-year term.

Reform the tax system so that work pays more, pay out toeslagen (income-dependent allowances) automatically and directly, introduce one national payment day for all income schemes, and abolish the kostendelersnorm (the cut in social assistance for adults sharing a home).

recent_developments.event: During the formation, informateur Sybrand van Haersma Buma (CDA), appointed on 13 November 2025, presented an interim report in which D66 and CDA agreed on five topics: migration, housing, security and defence, nitrogen, and the economy and investment climate.
The CDA supported a D66 bill requiring parties to admit members; party leader Bontenbal said: "Niemand is onaantastbaar" ("Nobody is untouchable").

D66, VVD and CDA presented the coalition agreement 'Aan de slag' ('Getting to work') for a minority cabinet with 66 of 150 House seats. NOS reported that Bontenbal wanted to remain House group leader and not become a minister.

The Jetten cabinet was sworn in and the CDA returned to government, supplying 5 ministers and 3 state secretaries. Bart van den Brink became Minister of Asylum and Migration and deputy prime minister; Tom Berendsen became Minister of Foreign Affairs and former group leader Pieter Heerma Minister of the Interior.
Former CDA leader and former minister Elco Brinkman died.

CDA and D66, without coalition partner VVD, backed an amendment by PRO and Volt to the 2027 Tax Plan shifting about 1 billion euros in taxation from labour to wealth, which the cabinet had advised against. The Tax Plan passed the House by 76 votes to 74, with the VVD voting against.

Deputy prime minister Bart van den Brink (CDA) said the events around the Tax Plan had put cooperation in the coalition under pressure, adding: "Want ik geloof dat als je in Nederland in het landsbestuur zit, je een zware verantwoordelijkheid draagt om de samenwerking op te zoeken" ("Because I believe that if you are in national government in the Netherlands, you bear a heavy responsibility to seek cooperation").

Prime Minister Jetten wrote to the House that the coalition continues in the same composition. Sybrand van Haersma Buma, the former CDA leader who is vice-president of the Council of State, was asked to report within a month on agreements about financial frameworks and procedural rules.
